html:
SMTO-CTR-0018 — The model's answer wasn't a usable task plan

GUID: 6c8da1a8-497a-4336-a085-4be214d577c4
Slug: task-contract-submission-invalid
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • SMTO asked its model (the AI service it uses) to write a plan for your request, but the answer came back in the wrong form, so SMTO couldn't use it. SMTO didn't act on your request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Retry on the task, or Retry contract generation in the Task contract step. Do this once. The model's answers vary, so one fresh attempt often comes back in the right form.
  2. If it fails again the same way, ask the person who manages SMTO to check the model under Settings › Setup › Model routing. Repeated badly formed answers usually mean the chosen model can't reliably reply in the form SMTO needs.
  3. Ask them to turn on Automatic Task Contract recovery under Settings › Agent behavior › Task Contracts. SMTO then retries badly formed answers by itself on new tasks.

What success looks like

  • The Task contract step shows Task contract generated and the task starts working.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with your request text, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep selecting Retry after the second failure; the same model will likely answer the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Task Contract compiler response did not contain exactly one smto__submit_task_contract tool call, or a combined capability-selection submission wrapped task_contract in a non-object value.

What this means

  • Compiler output contains other than one required submission tool call, uses the wrong tool name, or wraps task_contract in a non-object payload. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • Compiler output contains other than one required submission tool call, uses the wrong tool name, or wraps task_contract in a non-object payload.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the saved tool envelope/name/argument shape; ordinary task wording may already be valid.

How to fix it

  • Open the failed attempt's 'Generated output' and 'Why this attempt was rejected' in the Task contract activity; _run_compiler_attempt requires exactly one smto__submit_task_contract call and, with combined capability selection, an object task_contract. The failure is auto-retried when Automatic Task Contract recovery is enabled; if it repeats, the compiler model or endpoint likely lacks reliable required tool calling, so check the route under Settings > Setup > Model routing before another attempt.
  • Use the existing compiler correction/retry flow and inspect the provider submission contract if the failure repeats.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported compiler attempt returns exactly the required submission form.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
